name: Integris Medtech
summary: Integris Medtech makes cardiovascular devices such as drug-eluting stents and supplies laboratory equipment, reagents and services under the BioCal brand, with plants in India, Germany and the Netherlands and about two-thirds of revenue from outside India. Revenue grew from ₹1,348 cr in FY23 to ₹1,902 cr in FY25 and the company swung from a ₹4.9 cr loss to a ₹70.7 cr profit in FY25, but ROE was only 5.35% and borrowings tripled over the period. About ₹510 cr, or 85% of the ₹600 cr fresh issue, goes to repaying subsidiaries' borrowings, with nothing for new capacity, and the promoter Evercure Holdings is selling 1.08 crore shares. The price band was not announced when this was researched, so valuation checks are not rated and all figures come from the DRHP and its October 2026 addendum, not an RHP.

fh1.finding: Revenue from operations rose from ₹1,348.1 cr (FY23) to ₹1,902.5 cr (FY25), a CAGR of about 18.8%.

fh2.finding: Revenue grew every year: ₹1,348 cr, ₹1,553 cr, ₹1,902 cr (FY23–FY25).

fh3.finding: Debt to equity was about 0.20 at June 2025 (borrowings ₹793.4 cr vs net worth ₹3,890.0 cr).

fh4.finding: Borrowings rose 211% (₹556.5 cr to ₹1,729.5 cr) while revenue rose 41% over FY23–FY25; they fell to ₹793.4 cr by June 2025.

fh5.finding: Net worth rose every year: ₹2,629.5 cr, ₹2,681.0 cr, ₹2,752.5 cr (FY23–FY25).

fh6.finding: Operating cash flow was ₹155.5 cr in FY25, more than twice the ₹70.7 cr profit.

pr1.finding: Profit after tax turned from a ₹4.9 cr loss in FY24 to a ₹70.7 cr profit in FY25.

pr2.finding: Net margin improved from losses in FY23 (−₹40.5 cr) and FY24 (−₹4.9 cr) to 3.72% in FY25.

pr5.finding: Peer margins were not found in public sources.

va1.finding: The price band was not announced, so the post-issue P/E cannot be worked out; DRHP peers trade at 54.0x–56.0x.

va2.finding: The price band was not announced, so the post-issue price to book cannot be worked out.

va3.finding: The price band was not announced, so market cap to sales cannot be worked out.

va4.finding: No share issues or transfers in the 12 months before the IPO, or their prices, were found in public sources.

pg1.finding: Promoters hold 83.24% before the issue; the post-issue holding is not published yet.

pg2.finding: No information on pledged promoter shares was found.

pg3.finding: Related-party transaction figures were not found in public sources.

pg4.finding: A ₹15.09 cr regulatory proceeding involving promoter Gurmit Singh Chugh has been paid in full, with a closure report awaited.

is1.finding: The OFS of 1.08 crore shares has no rupee value until the price band is set, so its share of the issue is unknown.

is2.finding: Issue size and market cap are unknown until the price band is set.

is3.finding: Evercure Holdings is selling shares, but its average acquisition cost was not found.

up1.finding: None of the ₹600 cr fresh issue funds capex or expansion; it goes to repaying borrowings and general corporate purposes.

up2.finding: ₹509.85 cr, or about 85% of the ₹600 cr fresh issue, goes to repaying subsidiaries' borrowings.

up3.finding: The general corporate purposes amount is not stated; at most about ₹90 cr is left before expenses.

up4.finding: Public sources don't say whether any repaid loans are owed to promoters or group companies.

lg1.finding: Tax and regulatory claims against subsidiaries total about ₹17.5 cr, under 1% of the ₹3,890 cr net worth.

lg2.finding: One regulatory proceeding against promoters (₹15.09 cr) is paid in full and awaiting closure; no criminal cases against the company are reported.

lg3.finding: Contingent liabilities were not found in public sources.

rk1.finding: Top-10 customer share was not found in public sources.

rk2.finding: It works with over 200 suppliers, but supplier concentration figures were not found.

rk3.finding: Incorporated in 2008, so about 18 years of operating history.

rk4.finding: Auditor Walker Chandiok reports no unaddressed qualifications, but whether there is an emphasis of matter was not found.
